newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Robinson elected new Trinidad & Tobago president.
newsitem.headline: Robinson elected new Trinidad & Tobago president.

text.p: Former prime minister A.N.R. (Ray) Robinson was elected the next president of Trinidad and Tobago on Friday, the House of Representatives speaker announced.
He will take the oath of office on March 19 after incumbent President Noor Hassanali retires.
Speaker Hector McClean announced the results of balloting by an Electoral College members of the House and the Senate.
Robinson received 46 ballots and his challenger, high court judge Anthony Lucky, polled 18. One ballot was rejected.
It was the first time in the Caribbean state's history that an election was necessary for the head of state's post. Previously, the choice was unanimous.
This time, opposition leader Patrick Manning raised objections, saying that Robinson was an active politician and was unfit for the job.
Robinson, 70, was prime minister from 1986 to 1991.
